bullets.text: Real GDP growth projections have been revised downward to 5.1 percent in 2025 and 5.6 percent in 2026 following a sharper-than-expected third-quarter slowdown, while inflation is projected to average 1.7 percent in 2025 before rising to 2.8 percent in 2026.

Risks to the growth outlook remain tilted to the downside from trade policy uncertainty and severe weather, as demonstrated by the third-quarter 2025 growth slowdown to 4.0 percent following severe typhoons.

The fiscal deficit reached 5.7 percent of GDP in 2024 with national government debt at 60.7 percent of GDP, while authorities plan a gradual consolidation path to narrow the deficit to 5.5 percent of GDP in 2025 and 3.1 percent by 2030.

Monetary policy has appropriately shifted to an accommodative stance following 175 basis points of policy rate cuts since August 2024, with staff projecting an additional 50-basis-point reduction by the first quarter of 2026 to address an emerging negative output gap.

Systemic financial risk remains moderate, underpinned by well-capitalized banks with consolidated capital adequacy ratios of 16.6 percent in March 2025 and a contained banking system non-performing loan ratio of 3.3 percent as of end-June 2025.

The external position in 2024 was assessed to be weaker than implied by medium-term fundamentals, with the current account deficit reaching 4.0 percent of GDP in 2024 and gross international reserves standing at US$106 billion at end-2024.
